reasoning: Both are correct, fully torn down, well-typed classes that reuse PlacementRules. A's failed disconnect check is a heuristic miss: UnbindFromRenderStep correctly stops the frame update. A follows the project's Module convention, keeps its defaults as module-level constants that callers can't change, orders the update after the camera, and recolours only when placeability changes. B reads Material from BlockTypes and returns a reason, but it breaks the Module convention, re-applies the style every frame, and exposes defaults that callers can change. On balance A is slightly more merge-ready.

criteria.note: BindToRenderStep at Camera+1 raycasts from GetMouseLocation excluding part and character, snaps `result.Position + result.Normal * BlockSize/2`, hides on miss, and checks against PlacedBlocks; it only applies Color from BlockTypes and hardcodes SmoothPlastic.
Destroy guards with _IsDestroyed, calls UnbindFromRenderStep with a unique GUID name, and destroys the part, so no frame update runs afterwards.
All fields are declared in `typeof(setmetatable({} :: {...}, Module))` and set together in new; the part has CanCollide/CanQuery false and is in the raycast filter.
new(blockType: BlockType, options: GhostPreviewOptions?): GhostPreview, and GetPlacement returns (boolean, Vector3?) with the cell nil on a sky miss.
A GhostPreviewOptions table with Transparency/RaycastDistance falls back to the DEFAULT_TRANSPARENCY and DEFAULT_RAYCAST_DISTANCE constants.
One file, no controller or input code, and lsp/selene/stylua all pass; it follows the Module naming convention.

A RenderStepped raycast excludes the part and character, applies the half-block normal offset before snap, hides on miss, and _applyStyle uses both style.Material and Color with a red tint when check fails.
destroy disconnects _connection, nils it, and destroys the part; it is safe to call repeatedly.
Fields are declared in `type self` and cast in the constructor and the part is non-queryable, but the lowercase `self` type name and the public mutable defaults on the class table are a bit untidy.
getPlacement returns (boolean, Vector3?, string?), the parameters use BlockType, and the constructor return is typed.
Uses an Options table, but the defaults are GhostPreview.DefaultTransparency fields that callers can change rather than local constants.
In scope and the checks pass, but it misses the Module class-table convention.

strengths: Clean render-step binding with a unique name and priority after the camera
Idempotent Destroy with a destroyed flag
Consistent naming matching the project convention
weaknesses: Ghost isn't positioned until the first frame (minor)

strengths: Takes the full style (Material and Color) from BlockTypes
Also exposes the reason a spot is blocked
Runs an immediate first update in the constructor
weaknesses: Defaults can be changed through the class table
